title: This is my ball: Tämä on minun palloni
summary: Use Tämä on … to identify a thing as someone’s: Tämä on minun palloni means “This is my ball”.
objectives: Identify one thing as someone’s using Tämä on and a possessive phrase.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Use Tämä on … to identify a thing as someone’s: Tämä on minun palloni means “This is my ball”.
Tämä means “this”; on means “is” in this identity sentence. It describes the one thing, even when the owner is meidän or heidän. The possessive phrase has the owner form and its matching noun ending.
keyPoints: This is my ball: Tämä on minun palloni
Practise one singular possessed thing with the supporting forms shown.

steps: Begin with Tämä (“this”) + on (“is”) to identify one thing.
Minun (“my”) chooses -ni: pallo (“ball”) + -ni = palloni. Put the owner phrase after on.
Keep Tämä on (“This is”) at the beginning.
Sinun means “your” for one person: kirja (“book”) + -si = kirjasi. Put sinun before the possessed noun.
Tämä on identifies one pen. Hänen means “her” or “his”; this example uses “her”.
Kynä (“pen”) has front vowels: kynä + -nsä = kynänsä. Retain hänen to name the single owner in this frame.
Tämä on describes one car, even though meidän (“our”) names several owners.
Auto (“car”) + -mme = automme; use on for the one thing being identified.
Teidän means “your” for a group here. Begin with Tämä on (“This is”).
Peli (“game”) + -nne = pelinne. First-/second-person endings do not switch to -nsa/-nsä for vowel harmony.
Heidän means “their”; the frame still identifies one pillow with Tämä on.
Tyyny (“pillow”) + -nsä = tyynynsä because the noun has front vowels. Retain heidän to name the group of owners.

commonMistakes: Tämä on identifies one thing, so keep on even when meidän or heidän names several owners.
Keep the complete matching possessive phrase when the task requests the owner pronoun: Tämä on meidän automme.
The noun ending identifies its owner; it does not make the possessed thing plural.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “This is their ball.” Keep the owner pronoun. Use heidän pallonsa (“their ball”), tämä (“this”), and on (“is”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Place the complete owner phrase after Tämä on; keep its pronoun before the noun.

parts.formation: Tämä is the supplied basic singular word for “this”.
Olla uses on because the thing being identified is singular; the owner can still be plural.
Use the learned genitive form: heidän. Genitive means the form naming whose thing it is.
pallo + -nsa = pallonsa. The ending marks the owner, not several things.
